items.stem: In modern SharePoint, what is the recommended way to connect a family of related sites?

options.text: Associate them with a hub site
options.rationale: Correct: hub sites connect related sites while keeping a flat architecture.

options.text: Create nested subsites under one site collection
options.rationale: Subsites are not recommended in the modern flat architecture.

options.text: Put all content in one giant document library
options.rationale: A single library does not connect sites and harms findability.
Permissions do not connect sites and this violates least privilege.

items.explanation: Correct: hub sites connect related sites while keeping a flat architecture.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO practices follow Microsoft's SharePoint permissions guidance? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Follow the principle of least privilege
options.rationale: Correct: least privilege is a core SharePoint permissions guideline.

options.text: Use the default Members, Visitors and Owners groups
options.rationale: Correct: using standard groups and controlling at site level is recommended.

options.text: Assign permissions to individual users wherever possible
options.rationale: Incorrect: Microsoft recommends groups over individual users.

options.text: Break inheritance on every list and item by default
options.rationale: Incorrect: extensive fine-grained permissions increase management burden and are discouraged.

items.explanation: Correct: least privilege and standard groups are the recommended practices.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: What happens when you stop inheriting permissions on a document library?

options.text: It copies the parent's groups and permissions, then breaks the link so later parent changes do not flow down
options.rationale: Correct: breaking inheritance copies current permissions and then decouples the child.

options.text: It immediately removes all existing permissions from the library
options.rationale: Existing permissions are copied, not removed.
Breaking inheritance does not delete content.

options.text: It grants every user Full Control
options.rationale: It does not change permission levels to Full Control.

items.explanation: Correct: breaking inheritance copies current permissions and then decouples the child from the parent.
